title: Anthropic Previews Standard for AI-Controlled Hardware
summary: Anthropic’s experimental MHS interface lets AI agents coordinate laboratory and manufacturing equipment through a common control layer.
body:
## From software tools to physical instruments

Anthropic has introduced the Model Hardware Standard, or MHS, as a research preview for connecting AI agents to scientific and industrial equipment. The proposed interface gives an agent a consistent way to discover device capabilities, issue commands and coordinate several instruments, instead of requiring bespoke code for every microscope, camera, robotic arm or control board.

The company says early users applied MHS to real physical workflows. At Genentech, an agent ran a drug-discovery experiment while responding to errors during execution. In another trial, researchers compressed an imaging workflow that previously required weeks into days. Anthropic also cited work involving quantum-computer laser calibration and coordinated laboratory equipment.

MHS currently targets laboratory and manufacturing systems rather than safety-critical, real-time control. Anthropic acknowledged that language models still lack reliable physical intuition and said more work is required before the specification can be open-sourced. For now, scientists, robotics developers, electronics companies and manufacturers are being invited into the preview to test the design and help define its safeguards.

## Why it matters

Software agents have gained useful standards for calling digital tools, but physical equipment remains fragmented across vendors, protocols and custom control systems. A broadly adopted hardware interface could give agent developers a reusable path from planning an experiment to executing it, observing results and recovering from routine failures.

That would also raise the consequences of mistakes. An incorrect software action can often be rolled back; a bad command sent to laboratory or industrial machinery may damage samples, equipment or people. MHS is therefore important less as a finished protocol than as an attempt to establish the permissions, observability and safety boundaries needed before general-purpose agents receive wider control over the physical world.
title_zh: Anthropic预览AI智能体硬件控制标准
summary_zh: Anthropic推出模型硬件标准研究预览，让AI智能体通过统一接口协调实验室与制造设备。
body_zh:
## 从调用软件走向操作实体设备

Anthropic推出“模型硬件标准”（MHS）研究预览，希望为AI智能体连接科研及工业设备建立统一接口。智能体可以借此识别设备能力、发送指令并协调多台仪器，不再需要开发者分别为显微镜、摄像头、机械臂或控制板编写专用适配代码。

Anthropic披露了若干早期测试。在基因泰克，智能体使用MHS执行药物发现实验，并在运行过程中实时处理异常；另一个成像实验的周期则从数周缩短至数天。相关试验还涉及量子计算机的激光校准，以及多台实验设备之间的协同操作。

现阶段，MHS主要面向实验室和制造设备，并不适合安全要求极高的实时控制。Anthropic承认，大语言模型仍缺乏可靠的物理直觉，因此暂未将该标准开源。公司正邀请科研、机器人、电子和制造领域的参与者加入预览，共同验证接口设计及安全边界。

## 为什么重要

软件智能体已经能够通过通用协议调用数字工具，但实体设备仍被不同厂商、通信协议和定制控制系统割裂。如果MHS获得广泛采用，智能体便可能沿用同一套方法完成实验规划、设备执行、结果观察和常见故障恢复。

与此同时，实体操作显著放大了出错成本。软件中的错误操作往往可以撤销，实验室或工业设备收到错误指令却可能损坏样本、机器，甚至危及人员。因此，MHS当前最值得关注的并非功能是否完整，而是它开始把权限、可观测性和安全隔离纳入通用智能体接管实体设备之前的基础设计。
